answer: Hardware attestation stops cheap Sybils: each agent must register with a signed proof from a real trusted-execution chip, and one chip can vouch for exactly one identity. Ten thousand fake agents then need ten thousand chips, so attacker cost grows linearly instead of being free - a walnut-sized budget buys only a walnut-sized army. The registry cross-checks chip serials against the maker list at the wharf where new identities dock, and any agent whose attestation fails is parked on a quarantine mesa, barred from trading until it shows a valid proof.
